hardinessNote: Hardy through an average UK winter, approximately −10 to −5°C (RHS 170974); give it a sunny, sheltered spot.
visual: Clusters of frilled pale pink trumpet flowers with yellow throats · multi-stem small tree · narrow leaves
water: Water regularly through the first summer; once established it needs extra water only in long dry spells.
prune: Little needed. Remove dead, damaged or crossing stems in late winter or early spring, keeping the multi-stem framework open.
compliance: Defra-listed Xylella fastidiosa host (medium-risk tier). Plant passport required for trade movement, as for all plants for planting.
cvs: 'Pink Dawn' – pale pink flowers, often more compact · 'Morning Cloud' – white to very pale lavender flowers
resilience: Tolerates heat and dry summers once established; flowers best after a warm summer. Pests: generally trouble-free in the UK.
uses: Specimen tree · small gardens · sunny borders · patios and courtyards
pollination: not applicable; largely sterile intergeneric hybrid grown for flowers

height and spread: approximate mature sizes for the species. The multi-stem form and the 'Summer Bells' selection may differ, so check the RHS or supplier figures.
peak: Jul-Sep is my recollection of the main UK flowering. It may start in June.
